Core Active Vocabulary (14 items):

head — the top part of the body. Example: Put your hand on your head.
eyes — the parts of the face you see with. Example: Her eyes are blue.
hair — what grows on your head. Example: She has got long brown hair.
face — the front of your head. Example: He has got a friendly face.
body — the whole physical person. Example: Sport is good for the body.
tall — of more than average height. Example: My brother is tall.
short — of less than average height, or not long. Example: She is short with dark hair.
young — not old. Example: He is young and energetic.
old — having lived a long time. Example: My grandfather is old.
beautiful — very pleasant to look at. Example: She has a beautiful face.
handsome — good-looking, usually about a man. Example: He is a handsome young man.
black — the colour of night. Example: He has got black hair.
brown — the colour of wood or coffee. Example: Her hair is brown.
blue — the colour of the sky. Example: My eyes are blue.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• What does he look like?
• She has got ... hair.
• He is tall.
• Her eyes are blue.
• He is young.

elements.content: Stress the adjective, not the noun.
She has got LONG hair and BLUE eyes.
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word carries the main stress?
Grammar focus: Adjectives (adjective + noun).
Put the adjective before the noun: long hair, blue eyes. After the verb be, put it after: Her hair is long. Use has got for hair and eyes.
